hypothesis: Reverting angular_momentum_reward_weight to -0.01 while retaining the stronger gait_phase_regularity_reward_weight (-2.5) and looser shoulder_pitch tolerance (0.35) isolates whether the gait regularity penalty alone can drive CV metrics toward the healthy range. The previous run's stability failure is attributed primarily to the 5× angular momentum penalty increase conflicting with torso dynamics needed for balance — removing that change should restore stability while keeping the two changes most likely to improve gait rhythm and arm naturalness.
expected_effects: fell_over_rate drops back below 0.5 — stability restored by removing the aggressive angular momentum penalty
gait_air_cv_mean and gait_contact_cv_mean decrease toward <0.2 — direct effect of the stronger regularity penalty now able to act without competing destabilization
track_linear_velocity reward decreases slightly — expected Rule 6 side effect confirming regularity weight is doing work (if it doesn't dip, the penalty is not effective)
symmetry_vel_cost_mean improves — more periodic gait should reduce velocity asymmetry between legs
landing_force_mean remains in 30-90 N range — no soft_landing weight change, should be unaffected
